html:
Morija is a town in western Lesotho founded in 1833 as the first station of the Paris Evangelical Missionary Society, invited by Moshoeshoe I.

The French Protestant missionaries were welcomed as advisers as much as preachers. They wrote down the Sesotho language, opened schools and in 1861 set up a printing press, which from 1863 printed one of the first newspapers in an African language. Most Basotho became Christians over the following century.

The press published Sesotho books, among them Thomas Mofolo's novel Chaka. Lesotho has one of the highest literacy rates in Africa, a legacy of the mission schools of Morija and the church in Lesotho.
sum: Morija is a town in western Lesotho founded in 1833 as the first station of the Paris Evangelical Missionary Society, invited by Moshoeshoe I.
